Hi Elliot / Priya —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our call and the concrete next steps so we keep momentum: 

Key pain points you shared
- High variability in latency for short completions (customer-facing chat) leading to poor UX spikes.
- Cost sensitivity at scale — want to avoid large headroom on GPU fleet for steady-state.
- Need for a reproducible rollback path and clear observability for token-level cost.

Goals we heard
- P95 latency <= 250ms for short-chat prompts (<= 128 tokens) in production; P99 acceptable to be higher as long as fallbacks exist.
- Peak throughput target ~120 concurrent users generating ~30 requests/sec for peak region.
- Proof-of-concept (PoC) to validate latency, cost, and KV prefix caching over 4 weeks.

Immediate next steps (owner / ETA)
1) Redwood sends technical follow-up with recommended serving topology and quantization guidance — Ben (tomorrow, 3/15).
2) Hypertide shares sample prompt mix and expected token distribution (by EOD 3/16) — Priya.
3) Align on procurement/PO timeline and any required paperwork — Elliot / procurement.

Ben and Lauren are looped for the technical handoff. I attached the slide summary and an estimated QPS/latency spreadsheet to help frame the PoC.

Thanks — I’ll follow up after Ben’s technical note with a proposed PoC schedule and can pull together a one-page SOW draft if that helps procurement.

Best,

Subject: Hypertide — technical deep-dive (topology, SLOs, model guidance)

Elliot / Priya — tagging onto Jasmine’s thread with the technical handoff. Below is a concise, actionable set of recommendations for the PoC. If useful, we can expand any section into a runbook.

Executive summary
- Goal: Validate p95 latency <= 250ms for short-chat flows (<=128 tokens) at peak of 120 concurrent users. Target PoC duration: 4 weeks.
- Recommendation: Start PoC on Redwood Dedicated capacity in us-west-2 using 2x A100-equivalent nodes (dedicated pool) with autoscaling to 4 nodes for bursts.

Model & quantization guidance
- Primary model: Llama-3-70B (8-bit quantized q4f16) — balance of quality and performance.
- Fallback: Llama-3-13B quantized (faster KV cache reuse, lower memory).
- Tokenization: use shared tokenizer; expect ~1.2x tokens compared to naive counts for mixed-language prompts.

Serving topology
- Dedicated pool with autoscale policy: base=2 nodes, max=4, scale-on-p95-latency>220ms or queue length>10.
- Prefix/KV caching: enable prefix caching for repeated system prompts (internal rate ~35% repeated).
- Batching: dynamic batching with max batch size tuned to keep p95 under 250ms for short flows — start with target batch window 10ms.
- Smart routing: route short-chat traffic to higher-priority nodes with smaller batch windows; route long jobs to dedicated background queue.

SLOs and metrics to validate
- p95 latency (<= 250ms) for <=128-token completions.
- p50/p95 token/sec per GPU to be captured (baseline numbers in attached spreadsheet).
- Cost-per-1k tokens target: keep below $0.40 for PoC (estimate, see spreadsheet).
- Observability: token-level cost, per-request model variant, region, and kv-cache hit rate.

Runbook highlights for degradation
- If p95 spikes above 400ms: switch short-chat route to fallback model (13B) with degraded QoS and scale pool by +1 node.
- If queue length > 50 for >60s: enable burst capacity (pre-authorized) or shed non-critical background jobs.

PoC deliverables & timeline
- Day 0–3: infra prep (network allowlist, KMS handshake, test credentials).
- Day 4–10: synthetic load runs to tune batch windows and autoscale triggers.
- Week 2–4: run production-like traffic, collect metrics, iterate.

Required inputs from Hypertide
- Sample prompt distribution CSV (Priya)
- PO or short SOW to enable dedicated capacity (procurement@hypertide.co)
- Allowlist for IPs and KMS thumbprint (Tom)

Attachments: a small topology diagram and a QPS/latency estimate workbook were uploaded to the Drive link Jasmine shared.

Happy to jump on the follow-up — Thu 3/17 11:00AM PT works for me.

Ben Carter

Redwood Inference
